question: Find the missing number: 3, 7, 16, 35, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 74.

GIVEN

• Series: 3, 7, 16, 35, ?

SOLUTION

• Look at how each term is made from the previous one: 3 × 2 + 1 = 7; 7 × 2 + 2 = 16; 16 × 2 + 3 = 35.

• The number added increases by 1 each time (+1, +2, +3, …), so the next step is × 2 + 4.

• Missing number = 35 × 2 + 4 = 70 + 4 = 74.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• When the differences are 4, 9, 19, …, test "× 2 + n" with n = 1, 2, 3, 4: the next term is 35 × 2 + 4 = 74.

NOTE

• Option 1 (70) is wrong: it is 35 × 2 with nothing added.

• Option 3 (80) and Option 4 (88) are wrong: they do not follow the "× 2 + n" pattern (n must be 4 for the next term).

• Differences of the series: 4, 9, 19, 39, which are themselves following the "× 2 + 1" pattern (4 × 2 + 1 = 9, 9 × 2 + 1 = 19, 19 × 2 + 1 = 39), and 35 + 39 = 74 ✓.

question:
From the given alternative words, select the word which can be formed using the letters of the given word.

IMMEDIATELY
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. LIMITED.

GIVEN

• Given word: IMMEDIATELY = I, M, M, E, D, I, A, T, E, L, Y (11 letters: I×2, M×2, E×2, and D, A, T, L, Y once each).

SOLUTION

• Check each option letter by letter against the given word.

• DIALECT: needs the letter C, which is not in IMMEDIATELY. ✗

• LIMITED: L, I, M, I, T, E, D; I is needed twice and is available twice, and all other letters are available. ✓

• DIAMETER: needs the letter R, which is not in IMMEDIATELY. ✗

• DICTATE: needs the letter C (and T twice, but T is available only once). ✗

• So the word that can be formed is LIMITED.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• First look for a letter that is missing from the given word: C and R are absent, which removes DIALECT, DIAMETER and DICTATE at once.

NOTE

• Option 1 (DIALECT) fails because C is not available.

• Option 3 (DIAMETER) fails because R is not available.

• Option 4 (DICTATE) fails because C is not available (and T appears twice, but only once in the given word).

• In word formation questions, check both the letters and their frequency (a letter cannot be used more times than it appears).

question:
Read the three given statements carefully, followed by conclusions I and II. Determine which of the conclusions logically follow from the statements, ignoring any commonly known facts or real-world knowledge.

Statements:

All wheat are browns.

Some browns are sugar.

All sugar are whites.

Conclusions:

I. Some wheat are sugar.

II. Some whites are wheat.
option_2: Either conclusion I or II follows
option_3: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Neither conclusion I nor II follows.

GIVEN

• Statement 1: All wheat are browns (A-type). Statement 2: Some browns are sugar (I-type). Statement 3: All sugar are whites (A-type).

SOLUTION

• Venn diagram: draw the circle "wheat" completely inside "browns". Draw "sugar" so that it overlaps (cuts) "browns", and draw "sugar" completely inside "whites".

• Conclusion I (Some wheat are sugar): the overlapping part of "browns" and "sugar" may lie entirely outside "wheat" (wheat is only a part of browns). So it is only a possibility, not definite. Does not follow.

• Conclusion II (Some whites are wheat): whites are linked with wheat only through sugar, and wheat may not touch sugar at all. So it is not definite. Does not follow.

• Neither conclusion follows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Syllogism rule: A + I gives no definite conclusion (All wheat are browns + Some browns are sugar → no relation between wheat and sugar). So any conclusion that joins wheat with sugar or whites is only a possibility.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Only conclusion I follows) is wrong: wheat and sugar need not overlap.

• Option 2 (Either I or II follows) is wrong: the "either-or" case applies only when the two conclusions are complementary (such as a pair "Some … are …" and "No … are …") and the case is a definite possibility; these two conclusions are not complementary.

• Option 4 (Only conclusion II follows) is wrong: wheat and whites need not overlap.

• Remember: A + I → no conclusion; A + A → A; I + A → I.

question: Select the option which is exactly similar to: Level 5, 480 Queen St, Brisbane QLD 4000, Australia; 31st March, '26
option_1: Level 5, 480 Queen St, Brisbane QLD 4000, Australia; 31st March, '26
option_2: Level 5, 480 Queen St., Brisbane QLD 4000, Australia; 31st March, '26
option_3: Level 5, 480 Queen St, Brisbane QLD 4000, Australia; 31st March, 26
option_4: Level 5, 480 Queen St, Brisbane QLD 4000, Australia; 31st March, ‘25
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Level 5, 480 Queen St, Brisbane QLD 4000, Australia; 31st March, '26.

GIVEN

• Given text: Level 5, 480 Queen St, Brisbane QLD 4000, Australia; 31st March, '26

SOLUTION

• Compare each option with the given text part by part (level, street, city, code, country, date).

• Option 1: every word, number and punctuation mark is the same as in the given text. ✓

• Option 2: "St." has a full stop after "St" (the given text has "St" without a full stop). ✗

• Option 3: the year is written as 26 without the apostrophe ('26 in the given text). ✗

• Option 4: the year is '25 instead of '26. ✗

• So the exactly similar option is Option 1.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Check in a fixed order: number → street → full stops → comma positions → code → country → date and year. A single difference rejects the option.

NOTE

• Option 2 differs by the extra full stop after "St".

• Option 3 differs by the missing apostrophe before 26.

• Option 4 differs by the year (25 instead of 26).

• In "exactly similar" questions, even a punctuation mark can make an option wrong.

question:
Which of the following addresses are identical?

1. Neha Sharma B-202, Lotus Apartments, Pune, 411001

2. Neha Sharma B-202, Lotus Apartment, Pune, 411001

3. Neha S. B-202, Lotus Apartments, Puna, 411001

4. Neha Sharma B-202, Lotus Apartments, Pune, 411001
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 1 and 4.

GIVEN

• Four addresses 1 to 4 are given. We have to find the two that are identical.

SOLUTION

• Compare the addresses part by part (name, flat number, building, city, PIN code).

• Address 1: Neha Sharma B-202, Lotus Apartments, Pune, 411001.

• Address 2: "Lotus Apartment" (singular) instead of "Lotus Apartments". ✗ (different from 1 and 4)

• Address 3: "Neha S." instead of "Neha Sharma" and "Puna" instead of "Pune". ✗

• Address 4: Neha Sharma B-202, Lotus Apartments, Pune, 411001, which is the same as address 1. ✓

• So addresses 1 and 4 are identical.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Find the odd ones out first: address 2 differs in "Apartment", address 3 differs in the name and in "Puna". The two that remain (1 and 4) must be identical.

NOTE

• Option 1 (1 and 3) is wrong: address 3 has "Neha S." and "Puna".

• Option 2 (2 and 3) is wrong: both addresses differ from each other and from addresses 1 and 4.

• Option 4 (3 and 4) is wrong: address 3 differs from 4 in the name and city.

question: Look at the matrix and choose the number from the options that should go in place of the question mark:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 74.

GIVEN

• Matrix: Row 1 = 4, 3, 25; Row 2 = 9, 2, 85; Row 3 = 7, 5, ?.

SOLUTION

• Row 1: 4² + 3² = 16 + 9 = 25. Row 2: 9² + 2² = 81 + 4 = 85.

• So in each row, the third number = (first number)² + (second number)².

• Row 3: 7² + 5² = 49 + 25 = 74.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Squares to remember: 4² = 16, 7² = 49, 9² = 81. Add the squares of the first two numbers in each row.

NOTE

• Option 1 (85) is the third number of Row 2, not Row 3.

• Option 2 (67) and Option 4 (95) are wrong: 49 + 25 = 74, not 67 or 95.

• In matrix questions, test the simple operations (sum, difference, product, squares) in each row and column.

question: Complete the series: CMX, FOW, IRV, ____, OAT.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. LVU.

GIVEN

• Series: CMX, FOW, IRV, ____, OAT.

SOLUTION

• First letters: C, F, I, ?, O → each moves +3 (C → F → I → L → O).

• Second letters: M, O, R, ?, A → the shifts are +2, +3, +4, +5. M (13) + 2 = O (15); O (15) + 3 = R (18); R (18) + 4 = V (22); V (22) + 5 = 27 = A (after Z, wrap around to A). So the missing letter is V.

• Third letters: X, W, V, ?, T → each moves −1 (X → W → V → U → T).

• The missing term is LVU.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Handle each position separately: +3, (+2, +3, +4, +5) and −1. Check the last term: O + 0 = O, V + 5 = A and U − 1 = T ✓.

NOTE

• Option 1 (SBK), Option 3 (RBK) and Option 4 (TBL) are wrong: their first letters do not follow the +3 pattern (I + 3 = L).

• Remember to wrap around after Z (27 → A, 28 → B).

question: Complete the series: BZA, DYC, FXE, ____, JVI.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. HWG.

GIVEN

• Series: BZA, DYC, FXE, ____, JVI.

SOLUTION

• First letters: B, D, F, ?, J → each moves +2 (B → D → F → H → J).

• Second letters: Z, Y, X, ?, V → each moves −1 (Z → Y → X → W → V).

• Third letters: A, C, E, ?, I → each moves +2 (A → C → E → G → I).

• The missing term is HWG.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Convert to numbers: (2, 26, 1), (4, 25, 3), (6, 24, 5), ?, (10, 22, 9). The pattern is +2, −1, +2, so the missing term is (8, 23, 7) = HWG.

NOTE

• Option 1 (HUG) is wrong: the middle letter would have to move −2.

• Option 3 (HWH) is wrong: the last letter would need to be H instead of G.

• Option 4 (GWH) is wrong: the first and last letters do not follow the +2 pattern.

question:
What will come in the place of '?' in the following equation, if '+' and '-' are interchanged and also 'x' and '÷' are interchanged?

40 x 10 - 20 + 10 ÷ 2 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 4.

GIVEN

• Interchange the signs: + ↔ − and × ↔ ÷. Equation: 40 × 10 − 20 + 10 ÷ 2 = ?

SOLUTION

• After interchanging, the equation becomes: 40 ÷ 10 + 20 − 10 × 2.

• Apply BODMAS (division and multiplication first): 40 ÷ 10 = 4 and 10 × 2 = 20.

• Now 4 + 20 − 20 = 4.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• First replace every sign by its partner, then solve by D–M–A–S. Do not solve the original equation.

NOTE

• Option 1 (8), Option 2 (6) and Option 3 (2) are wrong: they do not match 4 + 20 − 20.

• The value of the original equation (40 × 10 − 20 + 10 ÷ 2 = 400 − 20 + 5 = 385) is not what is asked; the signs must be interchanged first.

question: In the following question, a matrix of numbers is given. These numbers follow a certain pattern either row-wise or column-wise. Identify this pattern and choose the missing number accordingly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 4.

GIVEN

• Matrix: Row 1 = 8, 16, ?; Row 2 = 5, 20, 16; Row 3 = 6, 18, 9.

SOLUTION

• Row 2: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 and the third number is 16 = 4². Row 3: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 and the third number is 9 = 3².

• So in each row, (second number ÷ first number) = k and the third number = k².

• Row 1: 16 ÷ 8 = 2, so the missing number = 2² = 4.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Divide the middle number by the first number and square the answer: 16 ÷ 8 = 2 → 4.

NOTE

• Option 1 (9) is the third number of Row 3, not Row 1.

• Option 2 (16) is the third number of Row 2, not Row 1.

• Option 4 (36) would need the quotient 6, which does not match 16 ÷ 8 = 2.

question:
Choose the option that relates to the third term in the same way the second term relates to the first:

STORM : QVMTK :: CLOUD : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ANMWB.

GIVEN

• STORM : QVMTK :: CLOUD : ?

SOLUTION

• Compare STORM with QVMTK letter by letter: S → Q (−2), T → V (+2), O → M (−2), R → T (+2), M → K (−2).

• So the shifts alternate: −2, +2, −2, +2, −2.

• Apply the same shifts to CLOUD: C − 2 = A, L + 2 = N, O − 2 = M, U + 2 = W, D − 2 = B.

• The answer is ANMWB.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Write the pattern of shifts once (−2, +2, −2, +2, −2) and apply it to each position of the third word.

NOTE

• Option 1 (BKNTQ) and Option 4 (BJNRP) are wrong: their first letters are not C − 2 = A.

• Option 2 (AKMSR) is wrong: the second letter would have to be L + 2 = N, not K.

question: In a certain code language, the word CAPTAIN is written as CNIATPA. How will JOURNAL be written?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. JLANRUO.

GIVEN

• CAPTAIN → CNIATPA. Find the code of JOURNAL.

SOLUTION

• CAPTAIN: C-A-P-T-A-I-N. Code: C-N-I-A-T-P-A.

• The first letter (C) stays in its place, and the remaining six letters (A-P-T-A-I-N) are written in reverse order (N-I-A-T-P-A).

• Apply the same rule to JOURNAL: J stays; the remaining letters O-U-R-N-A-L reversed are L-A-N-R-U-O.

• The code is JLANRUO.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Keep the first letter and reverse the rest: J + (OURNAL reversed = LANRUO) = JLANRUO.

NOTE

• Option 1 (JLNAROU), Option 2 (JLARNUO) and Option 4 (JLNARUO) are wrong: each has the last six letters in a wrong order, not the reverse of O-U-R-N-A-L.

• Always check which positions stay fixed and which are reversed or shifted.

question: If 'A + B' means A is the father of B; 'A - B' means A is the sister of B; 'A × B' means A is the husband of B; and 'A ÷ B' means A is the mother of B. What does P + Q × R mean?
option_1: R is the daughter-in-law of P.
option_2: R is the daughter of P.
option_3: P is the brother-in-law of R.
option_4: P is the father of R.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. R is the daughter-in-law of P..

GIVEN

• A + B = A is the father of B; A − B = A is the sister of B; A × B = A is the husband of B; A ÷ B = A is the mother of B. Decode P + Q × R.

SOLUTION

• P + Q: P is the father of Q.

• Q × R: Q is the husband of R, so R is Q's wife.

• P is the father of Q, and R is the wife of Q (P's son). So R is the daughter-in-law of P.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Father → son → wife: the wife of one's son is the daughter-in-law. Q's gender is male because Q is a husband.

NOTE

• Option 2 (R is the daughter of P) is wrong: R is the wife of P's son, not P's own daughter.

• Option 3 (P is the brother-in-law of R) is wrong: P is R's father-in-law.

• Option 4 (P is the father of R) is wrong: P is R's father-in-law, not her father.

• Relations to remember: son's wife = daughter-in-law; husband's father = father-in-law.

question: If DARK is coded as kRaD, then how is WIND coded?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. dNiW.

GIVEN

• DARK → kRaD. Find the code of WIND.

SOLUTION

• The word DARK is first written in reverse order: K-R-A-D.

• The letters are then written alternately in small and capital form, starting with a small letter: k (small), R (capital), a (small), D (capital) = kRaD.

• Apply the same rule to WIND: reverse = D-N-I-W; the alternate small/capital form gives d (small), N (capital), i (small), W (capital) = dNiW.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Two steps: (1) reverse the letters; (2) write them in the pattern small–CAPITAL–small–CAPITAL.

NOTE

• Option 2 (DnIw) is wrong: it begins with a capital letter, but the pattern begins with a small letter.

• Option 3 (DniW) and Option 4 (dNIw) are wrong: they do not follow the alternating small and capital pattern.

question:
Instruction: The question given below is followed by two statements, I and II. Determine which statement(s) is/are sufficient to answer the question.

Question: Is G taller than H?

Statements:

I. G is taller than F, and F is taller than H.

II. H is not the shortest among G, H, F.
option_3: Both I and II together are sufficient
option_4: Either I or II is sufficient
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Only I is sufficient.

GIVEN

• Question: Is G taller than H? Statement I: G > F and F > H. Statement II: H is not the shortest among G, H and F.

SOLUTION

• Statement I: G > F and F > H, so G > F > H. Therefore G is taller than H. Sufficient.

• Statement II: H is not the shortest, so either F or G is the shortest. This does not tell whether G is taller than H (G could be the shortest). Not sufficient.

• So only statement I is sufficient.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Write the statements as a chain: Statement I gives G > F > H directly. If a statement alone gives a definite yes or no, it is sufficient.

NOTE

• Option 2 (Only II is sufficient) is wrong: statement II leaves the order of G and H open.

• Option 3 (Both I and II together are sufficient) is wrong: statement I is already sufficient, so the question is answered by it alone.

• Option 4 (Either I or II is sufficient) is wrong: statement II alone is not sufficient.

question:
In the following question, evaluate the statement and select the valid conclusion.

Statements:

I. Deficiency of iron in the human body causes anaemia.

II. Anaemia leads to weakness and fatigue.

Conclusions:

I. Iron-rich food should be included in the diet.

II. All weak people suffer from anaemia.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Only conclusion I follows..

GIVEN

• Statement I: Iron deficiency causes anaemia. Statement II: Anaemia leads to weakness and fatigue.

SOLUTION

• Conclusion I (Iron-rich food should be included in the diet): since iron deficiency causes anaemia, which leads to weakness, including iron-rich food prevents the problem. Follows.

• Conclusion II (All weak people suffer from anaemia): weakness can have many other causes; the statements only say that anaemia leads to weakness, not that all weakness is due to anaemia. Does not follow.

• So only conclusion I follows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Words like "all" in a conclusion are usually too strong. A conclusion that suggests a preventive step (a "should" based on the cause given in the statements) is usually valid.

NOTE

• Option 2 (Only conclusion II follows) is wrong: it reverses the cause and effect and uses the extreme word "all".

• Option 3 (Both follow) is wrong because conclusion II does not follow.

• Option 4 (Neither follows) is wrong because conclusion I follows. (The PDF shows this option as a red, wrong selection.)

question:
In the following question, evaluate the statement and select the valid conclusion.

Statements:

I. Bacteria can cause several infectious diseases.

II. Proper hygiene reduces the spread of bacteria.

Conclusions:

I. Maintaining cleanliness helps prevent infections.

II. All bacteria are harmful to humans.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Only conclusion I follows..

GIVEN

• Statement I: Bacteria can cause several infectious diseases. Statement II: Proper hygiene reduces the spread of bacteria.

SOLUTION

• Conclusion I (Maintaining cleanliness helps prevent infections): hygiene reduces the spread of bacteria, and bacteria cause infections, so cleanliness helps prevent infections. Follows.

• Conclusion II (All bacteria are harmful to humans): the statement says that bacteria "can cause" diseases (several), not that all are harmful. Does not follow.

• So only conclusion I follows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Combine the two statements for the first conclusion (hygiene → fewer bacteria → fewer infections). The word "all" in the second conclusion makes it too strong.

NOTE

• Option 2 (Only conclusion II follows) is wrong: "all bacteria are harmful" is an over-generalisation.

• Option 3 (Both follow) is wrong because conclusion II does not follow.

• Option 4 (Neither follows) is wrong because conclusion I follows.

question:
Read the statement and select the valid  assumptions given below.

Statement:

The growing use of online banking services has significantly decreased the length of queues at bank branches.

Assumptions:

I. A large number of customers today choose digital transactions instead of going to bank branches in person.

II. The main reason for long queues at bank branches was customers carrying out routine transactions physically at the branch.
option_3: Both I and II are implicit
option_4: Neither I nor II is implicit
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Both I and II are implicit.

GIVEN

• Statement: The growing use of online banking has significantly decreased the length of queues at bank branches.

SOLUTION

• An assumption is something that is taken for granted by the speaker in making the statement.

• Assumption I: queues have shortened because of online banking, which is possible only if many customers now choose digital transactions rather than visiting the branch. Implicit.

• Assumption II: for online banking to reduce queues, the queues must have been caused largely by routine transactions that customers performed in person at the branch (which can now be done online). Implicit.

• Both assumptions are implicit.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Ask: "Is this assumption necessary for the statement to be meaningful?" Here, the cause (online use) and the effect (shorter queues) work only if both assumptions hold.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Only assumption I is implicit) is wrong: assumption II is also taken for granted. (The PDF shows this option as a red, wrong selection.)

• Option 2 (Only assumption II is implicit) is wrong: assumption I is also implicit.

• Option 4 (Neither I nor II is implicit) is wrong: both are implied by the statement.

question:
In the following question, one statement is given, followed by certain inferences. Consider the statements to be true even if it seems to contradict commonly known facts. Read the inferences carefully and decide which of them logically follow(s) from the given statement.

Statement:

Regular exercise helps in maintaining good health.

Inferences:

I. People who exercise regularly are likely to be healthier than those who do not.

II. Lack of exercise may negatively affect a person’s health.
option_3: Both inference I and II follow
option_4: Neither inference I nor inference II follows
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Both inference I and II follow.

GIVEN

• Statement: Regular exercise helps in maintaining good health.

SOLUTION

• Inference I (People who exercise regularly are likely to be healthier than those who do not): if exercise helps maintain good health, regular exercisers are likely to be healthier. The word "likely" keeps it cautious. Follows.

• Inference II (Lack of exercise may negatively affect a person's health): if exercise helps maintain health, the lack of it may harm health. The word "may" keeps it cautious. Follows.

• Both inferences follow.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Inferences that use soft words such as "likely" and "may" and that restate the statement are usually valid, while those using "all", "only" and "always" are usually invalid.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Only inference I follows) is wrong: inference II also follows. (The PDF shows this option as a red, wrong selection.)

• Option 2 (Only inference II follows) is wrong: inference I also follows.

• Option 4 (Neither follows) is wrong: both inferences are supported by the statement.

question: Surya starts from point A and drives 7 km towards North. He then takes a right turn, drives 2 km to reach point B. He then turns right, drives 8 km and stops at point C. In which direction is point C with respect to point A?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. South-east.

GIVEN

• A → 7 km North; right turn → 2 km East (point B); right turn → 8 km South (point C).

SOLUTION

• Take A as the origin. After 7 km North he is 7 km north of A. After 2 km East he is at B (7 km north, 2 km east).

• A right turn from East is South; he drives 8 km South: the north–south position is 7 − 8 = 1 km, i.e. 1 km south of A's level. The east–west position stays 2 km east.

• So C is 2 km east and 1 km south of A, i.e. in the South-east direction of A.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Net movement: North 7 and South 8 → 1 km South; East 2 km. South + East = South-east.

NOTE

• Option 2 (North-west) is wrong: C is neither west nor north of A.

• Option 3 (South) is wrong: C is also 2 km to the east, so it is not exactly south.

• Option 4 (North-east) is wrong: the final position is south of A's level (8 km south after 7 km north).

• Distance of C from A = √(2² + 1²) = √5 km ≈ 2.24 km.

question:
Which of the mathematical signs should be interchanged in the below equation to make it mathematically correct?

 

192 - 16 + 18 × 6 ÷ 24 = 96
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. - and ÷.

GIVEN

• Equation: 192 − 16 + 18 × 6 ÷ 24 = 96. Find the pair of signs that should be interchanged.

SOLUTION

• Try Option 3 (− and ÷): the equation becomes 192 ÷ 16 + 18 × 6 − 24.

• 192 ÷ 16 = 12 and 18 × 6 = 108.

• 12 + 108 − 24 = 120 − 24 = 96 ✓ (the right-hand side).

• So the signs "−" and "÷" should be interchanged.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Check the options one by one. The original value is 192 − 16 + 4.5 = 180.5, which is far from 96, so a division must replace the first subtraction to bring down 192 (192 ÷ 16 = 12).

NOTE

• Option 1 (− and +): 192 + 16 − 18 × 6 ÷ 24 = 192 + 16 − 4.5 = 203.5 ≠ 96. ✗

• Option 2 (− and ×): 192 × 16 + 18 − 6 ÷ 24 is a very large number, not 96. ✗

question:
Akash and Rakesh are brothers. Omprakash is the father of Mahesh. Piyush is the brother of Kavya, and Kavya is the daughter of Rakesh.

 

How is Akash related to Piyush?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Uncle.

GIVEN

• Akash and Rakesh are brothers. Omprakash is the father of Mahesh (an unrelated statement for this question). Piyush is Kavya's brother, and Kavya is Rakesh's daughter.

SOLUTION

• Kavya is the daughter of Rakesh, and Piyush is Kavya's brother, so Piyush is Rakesh's son.

• Akash is Rakesh's brother, so Akash is the paternal uncle (chacha / tau) of Piyush.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Brother of the father = uncle. Akash → brother of Rakesh (Piyush's father) → uncle.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Father) is wrong: Piyush's father is Rakesh.

• Option 3 (Brother) is wrong: Akash is of the previous generation, being Rakesh's brother.

• Option 4 (Cousin) is wrong: cousins are the children of one's uncles or aunts; Akash is himself the uncle.

• The sentence about Omprakash and Mahesh is extra information that is not used to relate Akash and Piyush.

question:
In the following question, a statement is given, followed by possible conclusions. Choose the conclusion that logically follows.

Statement:

The recent rise in electric vehicle adoption has been driven by government incentives, environmental concerns, and advancements in battery technology.

Conclusion 1: Government incentives are the primary reason for the rise in electric vehicle adoption.

Conclusion 2: The adoption of electric vehicles is primarily due to advancements in battery technology and environmental awareness.
option_3: Both Conclusion 1 and Conclusion 2 are followed.
option_4: Neither Conclusion 1 nor Conclusion 2 is followed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Both Conclusion 1 and Conclusion 2 are followed..

GIVEN

• Statement: The rise in EV adoption has been driven by government incentives, environmental concerns and advancements in battery technology.

SOLUTION

• The statement lists three factors as drivers of EV adoption. Conclusion 1 names government incentives as a main reason. Follows (as per the key), since incentives are one of the listed drivers.

• Conclusion 2 names advancements in battery technology and environmental awareness as the main reasons. Follows (as per the key), since both are listed drivers.

• So both conclusions follow, as per the answer key of the PDF.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Each conclusion restates factors that the statement itself gives as drivers of the rise in EV adoption, so they are treated as supported by the statement.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Only Conclusion 1) is wrong: Conclusion 2 is also based on drivers named in the statement.

• Option 2 (Only Conclusion 2) is wrong: Conclusion 1 is also based on a driver named in the statement.

• Option 4 (Neither) is wrong as per the key.

• (Flagged: the word "primary" in both conclusions is stronger than the statement, which does not rank the three factors; the key follows the PDF.)

question:
In the following question, three statements are given, followed by four conclusions, I, II, III and IV. Consider the statements to be true even if they appear to contradict commonly known facts. Based on the given statements, determine which conclusion(s) logically follow. Choose your answer from the options provided.

Statements:

I. All triangles are polygons.

II. Some circles are triangles.

III. All squares are circles.

Conclusions:

I. All squares are polygons.

II. Some polygons are circles.

III. Some triangles are squares.

IV. All circles are polygons.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Only Conclusion II follows.

GIVEN

• Statement I: All triangles are polygons (A-type). Statement II: Some circles are triangles (I-type). Statement III: All squares are circles (A-type).

SOLUTION

• Venn diagram: triangles lie completely inside polygons. The circle "circles" overlaps (cuts) triangles, so the common part also lies inside polygons. The circle "squares" lies completely inside "circles", but may or may not touch triangles.

• Conclusion I (All squares are polygons): squares are inside circles, but only a part of circles lies inside polygons, so squares may lie outside polygons. Does not follow.

• Conclusion II (Some polygons are circles): the part of circles that overlaps triangles is inside polygons, so some circles are polygons, and by conversion some polygons are circles. Follows.

• Conclusion III (Some triangles are squares): squares need not overlap triangles. Does not follow.

• Conclusion IV (All circles are polygons): only some circles are triangles, so not all circles are polygons. Does not follow.

• Only Conclusion II follows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Rule: I + A → I (Some circles are triangles + All triangles are polygons → Some circles are polygons → Some polygons are circles). "All" conclusions cannot come after a "Some" statement.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Only Conclusion I) is wrong: squares need not be inside polygons, as the link goes through "circles", which is only partly inside polygons.

• Option 3 (Only Conclusion III) is wrong: no definite relation between triangles and squares.

• Option 4 (Only Conclusion IV) is wrong: only some circles are triangles.

• (The statements use geometrical figures only as labels; in this question, ignore real-world facts such as "a square is a polygon".)

question: Chabahar Port is located in which country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iran.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chabahar Port (चाबहार बंदरगाह) is located in the Sistan and Baluchestan province of Iran, on the Gulf of Oman (Makran coast) in the Indian Ocean.

 

• It is the only Iranian port with direct access to the ocean, and India is developing the Shahid Beheshti terminal there. India Ports Global Limited (IPGL) signed a 10-year contract to operate it in May 2024.

 

• It gives India a route to Afghanistan and Central Asia that bypasses Pakistan, and it is part of the International North–South Transport Corridor (INSTC).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pakistan's Gwadar Port (developed by China under CPEC) is only about 72 km west of Chabahar.

 

• India built the Zaranj–Delaram highway in Afghanistan, which connects with Chabahar through Iran.

 

NOTE

 

• Pakistan (Option 1) is wrong: Gwadar and Karachi are Pakistan's major ports, not Chabahar.

 

• Afghanistan (Option 2) is wrong: it is a landlocked country and has no seaports.

 

• Bangladesh (Option 4) is wrong: its main ports are Chattogram and Mongla.

question: What is India’s rank in the Human Development Index (HDI) 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 130th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the Human Development Report 2025 (released by the UNDP in May 2025, covering 2023 data), India ranked 130th out of 193 countries with an HDI value of 0.685, placing it in the medium human development category. (मानव विकास सूचकांक)

 

• India's HDI value has moved up from 0.676 in the previous report, and the rank improved by two places from 132nd.

 

• The HDI is based on three dimensions: health (life expectancy at birth), education (mean and expected years of schooling) and standard of living (GNI per capita).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Human Development Report is published by the UNDP (United Nations Development Programme). The idea of the HDI was developed by Mahbub ul Haq and Amartya Sen in 1990.

 

• HDI categories: very high (0.800 and above), high (0.700–0.799), medium (0.550–0.699), low (below 0.550).

 

NOTE

 

• 125th (Option 1), 128th (Option 2) and 135th (Option 4) are wrong: India's rank in the HDI 2025 was 130th.

question: What is the name of the life evaluation scale used in the World Happiness Report?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Cantril Ladder.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The World Happiness Report ranks countries using the Cantril Ladder (कैंट्रिल सीढ़ी), a life evaluation scale. People are asked to imagine a ladder with steps numbered 0 (the worst possible life) to 10 (the best possible life) and to say on which step they currently stand.

 

• The ranking is based on a three-year average of these responses (from the Gallup World Poll). Six factors explain the differences: GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom to make life choices, generosity and perceptions of corruption.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The report is published by the Wellbeing Research Centre at the University of Oxford with Gallup and the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN), around the International Day of Happiness (20 March).

 

NOTE

 

• The Likert Scale (Option 2) is wrong: it is a rating scale (strongly agree to strongly disagree) used in surveys, not the scale of the WHR.

 

• The Gini Coefficient (Option 3) is wrong: it measures income inequality.

 

• Human Development Scale (Option 4) is wrong: it is not a scale used by the WHR; the HDI is published by the UNDP.

question: The LVM3 rocket employed for the CMS-03 mission is classified under which launch vehicle class?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Heavy lift launch vehicle.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark-3, earlier known as GSLV Mk III) is ISRO's heavy lift launch vehicle (भारी भार वाहक प्रक्षेपण यान). It is a three-stage vehicle (two solid strap-on boosters S200, a liquid core stage L110 and a cryogenic upper stage C25).

 

• It was used for the CMS-03 communication satellite mission (LVM3-M5, launched from Sriharikota in November 2025). CMS-03 is a multi-band communication satellite of about 4,400 kg, the heaviest communication satellite launched from India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• LVM3 launched Chandrayaan-3 (14 July 2023) and OneWeb satellites. The PSLV is a medium-lift vehicle, and the SSLV (Small Satellite Launch Vehicle) is for small satellites.

 

• LVM3 can place about 4,000 kg in geosynchronous transfer orbit (GTO) and about 8,000 kg in low Earth orbit (LEO).

 

NOTE

 

• Small satellite launcher (Option 1) is wrong: this describes the SSLV.

 

• Medium lift rocket (Option 2) is wrong: this describes the PSLV.

 

• Reusable launch vehicle (Option 4) is wrong: LVM3 is an expendable vehicle, not a reusable one (ISRO's RLV-TD is a separate experimental programme).

question:
Fill in the blank:

According to Census 2011, approximately ___ of India's population resides in urban areas.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 31.16%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to Census 2011, 31.16% of India's population (about 377 million people) lived in urban areas, and the remaining 68.84% lived in rural areas. (शहरी जनसंख्या)

 

• The urban share was 27.81% in Census 2001, so it rose by about 3.35 percentage points in a decade.

 

• India's total population in 2011 was 1,210.8 million (121.08 crore).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Highest urban share among states: Goa (62.17%), then Mizoram, Tamil Nadu and Kerala; among Union Territories, Delhi (97.5%) and Chandigarh (97.25%). Lowest urban share: Himachal Pradesh (10.04%).

 

• Census 2011 was the 15th census since 1872, and the 7th after Independence. The next census is planned for 2027.

 

NOTE

 

• 25.34%, 28.45% and 35.21% (Options 1, 2 and 4) are wrong: the urban population share in Census 2011 was 31.16% (these values do not match any census figure).

question: Which type of tax acts as an automatic stabilizer by maintaining a fixed percentage of income?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Proportional tax.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A proportional tax (आनुपातिक कर) takes a fixed percentage of income from all taxpayers, whatever their income level (for example, a flat 10% on every income). Tax collections rise and fall automatically along with income, so the tax works as a built-in (automatic) stabilizer, as per the PDF key.

 

• Because the tax revenue changes along with income without any new government decision, it reduces swings in disposable income and so stabilises the economy during booms and slumps.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Types of taxes by rate: Progressive (rate rises with income, e.g. Indian income tax slabs), Proportional (flat rate) and Regressive (rate falls as income rises, so the poor bear a heavier burden).

 

• Other automatic stabilizers: unemployment benefits and the MGNREGA-type schemes, which increase spending automatically in a downturn.

 

NOTE

 

• Progressive tax (Option 1) is wrong: its rate rises with income, so it does not maintain a fixed percentage.

 

• Regressive tax (Option 3) is wrong: the effective burden decreases as income rises.

 

• Indirect tax (Option 4) is wrong: it is a tax on goods and services (GST, customs duty), not a tax on income.

 

• (Flagged: many textbooks name the progressive income tax as the main automatic stabilizer; the key follows the PDF and the "fixed percentage" wording in the question.)

question: Which policy tool directly influences aggregate demand through government spending?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fiscal policy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fiscal policy (राजकोषीय नीति) is the government's policy on taxation and public spending. By changing government expenditure and taxes, it directly affects aggregate demand in the economy.

 

• Expansionary fiscal policy (higher spending or lower taxes) raises demand during a slowdown, while contractionary policy (lower spending or higher taxes) reduces demand to control inflation.

 

• In India, the fiscal policy is presented in the Union Budget (Article 112) by the Finance Minister and is administered by the Ministry of Finance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Monetary policy is the policy of the RBI on the money supply and interest rates (repo rate, CRR, SLR). The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has 6 members, and was set up in 2016 under the RBI Act amendment.

 

• The FRBM Act, 2003 sets targets for the fiscal deficit.

 

NOTE

 

• Monetary policy (Option 1) is wrong: it works through the money supply and the interest rate, not through government spending.

 

• Industrial policy (Option 3) is wrong: it deals with industrial growth and regulation.

 

• Trade policy (Option 4) is wrong: it deals with exports, imports and tariffs.

question: What was the actual economic growth rate achieved during the Eighth Five-Year Plan (1992-97)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6.8%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Eighth Five-Year Plan (1992–97) had a target growth rate of 5.6%, while the actual growth achieved was about 6.8%, higher than the target. (आठवीं पंचवर्षीय योजना)

 

• It was launched under Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao after the 1991 economic reforms, with the main objective of human development, including full employment, and it was based on the "Rao–Manmohan model" of liberalisation.

 

• It was the first plan prepared after the New Economic Policy of 1991.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Plan facts: First Plan (1951–56) growth 3.6%; the Ninth Plan (1997–2002) target 6.5%; the Tenth Plan target 8%; the Eleventh Plan (2007–12) target 9%; the Twelfth Plan (2012–17) was the last, and the Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015.

 

NOTE

 

• 5.6% (Option 1) is wrong: it was the target of the Eighth Plan, not the actual growth.

 

• 6.0% (Option 2) is wrong: it does not match the actual growth.

 

• 8.0% (Option 4) is wrong: it was the Tenth Plan target, not the Eighth Plan's achievement.

question: The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 is applicable to which of the following?
option_1: Restricted only to civil court proceedings
option_2: All judicial proceedings and all executive inquiries
option_4: Restricted only to High and Supreme Courts
solution_text:
The correct answer is All judicial proceedings and courts-martial.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, with effect from 1 July 2024. Under Section 1, it applies to all judicial proceedings in or before any court, including courts-martial, but not to affidavits and arbitration proceedings. (भारतीय साक्ष्य अधिनियम)

 

• It deals with the rules about what facts can be proved, the admissibility of evidence (including electronic and digital records, which are now primary evidence) and the burden of proof.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam has 170 sections (the Evidence Act had 167). The other two new criminal laws are the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (replacing the IPC) and the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (replacing the CrPC).

 

NOTE

 

• Restricted only to civil court proceedings (Option 1) is wrong: it applies to criminal and civil proceedings both.

 

• All judicial proceedings and all executive inquiries (Option 2) is wrong: it does not apply to non-judicial executive inquiries.

 

• Restricted only to High and Supreme Courts (Option 4) is wrong: it applies to proceedings before any court.

question: Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, what is the defining feature of a "Zero FIR"?
option_1: A report where no specific suspect is named
option_2: A report filed regardless of the crime's jurisdiction
option_3: A report filed electronically without visiting a station
option_4: A report filed when no physical evidence exists
solution_text:
The correct answer is A report filed regardless of the crime's jurisdiction.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Zero FIR (जीरो एफआईआर) can be registered at any police station irrespective of the territorial jurisdiction where the offence took place. The police station that receives it registers the FIR with serial number 0 and transfers it to the police station that has jurisdiction.

 

• Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS), which replaced the CrPC from 1 July 2024, Section 173 provides for Zero FIR, and it must be transferred to the concerned police station within 24 hours.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The BNSS also allows e-FIR (information given electronically, to be signed by the informant within three days) and requires preliminary enquiry for certain offences (punishable with 3 to 7 years) within 14 days.

 

• The concept of Zero FIR was developed after the Justice Verma Committee recommendations (2012) following the Delhi gang-rape case.

 

NOTE

 

• A report where no specific suspect is named (Option 1) is wrong: this is an FIR against unknown persons, not a Zero FIR. (The PDF shows this option as a red, wrong selection.)

 

• A report filed electronically without visiting a station (Option 3) is wrong: this is an e-FIR.

 

• A report filed when no physical evidence exists (Option 4) is wrong: an FIR does not depend on evidence being available.

question: Which of the following rulers were responsible for the extension of Saka power in western India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhumaka and Nahapana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sakas (Scythians) of western India, known as the Western Kshatrapas, extended their power over Gujarat, Malwa and Maharashtra under Bhumaka and Nahapana (the first two Kshatrapa rulers of the Kshaharata family). Their capital was at Ujjain and Minnagara. (शक शासक)

 

• Nahapana was defeated by the Satavahana king Gautamiputra Satakarni, who restruck Nahapana's coins. Later, the Western Kshatrapa power was revived by Chastana, and Rudradaman I (c. 130–150 CE) was the most famous ruler.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Junagadh (Girnar) rock inscription of Rudradaman I (in Sanskrit, c. 150 CE) is the earliest long inscription in Sanskrit, and mentions the repair of the Sudarshana lake, which was built in the Mauryan period.

 

• The Shaka Era (78 CE) is used as the National Calendar of India; it is traditionally linked to Kanishka (Kushana).

 

NOTE

 

• Bhumaka and Chahara (Option 1) is wrong: Chahara is not named as a ruler responsible for the extension of Saka power as per the key (Bhumaka and Nahapana are the Kshaharata rulers).

 

• Nahapana and Rudraprajeet (Option 2) is wrong: Rudraprajeet is not a known ruler of this period as per the key.

 

• Rudradaman and Gautamiputra (Option 4) is wrong: Gautamiputra Satakarni was a Satavahana king and the opponent of the Sakas.

question: Assam contributes approximately how much to India’s total tea production?
solution_text:
The correct answer is About 50%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assam (असम) is India's largest tea-producing state and contributes about 50% (roughly half) of India's total tea production. Assam tea is grown mainly in the Brahmaputra valley and is known for its strong, malty flavour.

 

• India is the second-largest producer of tea in the world after China. The Tea Board of India (headquarters at Kolkata) was established under the Tea Act, 1953.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other tea-producing states: West Bengal (Darjeeling, Dooars and Terai), Tamil Nadu (Nilgiri) and Kerala. Darjeeling tea was the first Indian product to get a GI tag (2004).

 

• The tea plant needs a warm, humid climate with 150–300 cm of rainfall and well-drained slopes. The first tea garden in Assam was set up in the 1830s after Robert Bruce found the native tea plant.

 

NOTE

 

• About 45% (Option 1) is wrong: Assam's share is higher, at around half of the national production.

 

• About 30% (Option 2) is wrong: it is too low for Assam's share.

 

• About 75% (Option 4) is wrong: it is too high; West Bengal and the southern states also produce a large share.

question: Which of the following correctly describes the components and charges involved in the formation of a nucleosome?
option_1: Negatively charged RNA wrapped around a neutral histone octamer.
option_2: Positively charged DNA wrapped around a negatively charged histone hexamer.
option_3: Negatively charged DNA wrapped around a positively charged histone octamer.
option_4: Neutral DNA wrapped around a basic protein complex rich in Lysine and Arginine.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Negatively charged DNA wrapped around a positively charged histone octamer..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A nucleosome (न्यूक्लियोसोम) is the basic repeating unit of chromatin. It consists of about 146–147 base pairs of DNA wrapped around a core of eight histone proteins (a histone octamer): two molecules each of H2A, H2B, H3 and H4.

 

• DNA is negatively charged because of its phosphate groups, while histones are positively charged (basic) because they are rich in the basic amino acids lysine and arginine. The electrostatic attraction holds the DNA tightly around the octamer.

 

• The histone H1 binds to the linker DNA and helps in packing the nucleosomes further.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The structure is often described as "beads on a string" (seen under an electron microscope). The nucleosome concept was given by Roger Kornberg (1974).

 

• Chromatin is of two types: euchromatin (loosely packed, transcriptionally active) and heterochromatin (densely packed, inactive).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is wrong: nucleosomes involve DNA, not RNA, and histones are positively charged, not neutral.

 

• Option 2 is wrong: DNA is negatively charged (not positively), and the core is an octamer, not a hexamer.

 

• Option 4 is wrong: DNA is not neutral but negatively charged. (Histones are indeed rich in lysine and arginine, but the statement as a whole is wrong.)

question: The outer core of the Earth's interior exists in which physical state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Liquid state.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The outer core (बाह्य क्रोड) of the Earth lies between about 2,900 km and 5,150 km deep and is in a liquid (molten) state, made mainly of iron and nickel. S-waves (secondary seismic waves) cannot pass through it, which proves that it is liquid.

 

• The movement of the liquid outer core generates the Earth's magnetic field (geodynamo effect).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The inner core (5,150–6,371 km) is solid because of the extremely high pressure, even though its temperature is about 5,000–6,000°C.

 

• Earth's layers: crust (up to about 35 km), mantle (up to 2,900 km), outer core and inner core. The Gutenberg discontinuity separates the mantle from the core; the Lehmann discontinuity separates the outer and inner cores.

 

NOTE

 

• Solid state (Option 1) is wrong: only the inner core is solid.

 

• Gaseous state (Option 3) is wrong: there is no gaseous layer in the Earth's interior.

 

• Plasma state (Option 4) is wrong: the core is not in a plasma state.

question: The term "En Passant" is associated with which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chess.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• En passant (French for "in passing") is a special pawn capture in chess (शतरंज). If a pawn moves two squares forward from its starting position and lands beside an enemy pawn, the enemy pawn can capture it as if it had moved only one square. The capture must be made immediately on the next move.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chess facts: The board has 64 squares (32 light and 32 dark) and each player has 16 pieces. FIDE (Fédération Internationale des Échecs) governs the sport, and World Chess Day is celebrated on 20 July. Viswanathan Anand was India's first Grandmaster (1988).

 

• Other special chess moves: castling and pawn promotion.

 

NOTE

 

• Fencing (Option 1) is wrong: its terms are "foil", "épée", "sabre" and "lunge".

 

• Billiards (Option 3) is wrong: its terms are "cue", "break" and "pocket".

 

• Bridge (Option 4) is wrong: it is a card game with terms such as "trump", "bid" and "dummy".

question: Which term refers to a situation in Chess where a player is NOT in check but has no legal move available?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Stalemate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A stalemate (शह-मात रहित गतिरोध) is a situation in chess in which the player whose turn it is to move is not in check but has no legal move. The game ends in a draw.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Related terms: Checkmate (the king is in check and cannot escape; the game is won), Castling (a special move of the king and a rook), Gambit (an opening in which a player sacrifices material, usually a pawn, for an advantage).

 

NOTE

 

• Checkmate (Option 1) is wrong: here the king is in check with no escape (the PDF shows this option as a red, wrong selection).

 

• Castling (Option 3) is wrong: it is a move, not a game situation.

 

• Gambit (Option 4) is wrong: it is an opening strategy.

question: Who authored the book ‘Gulamgiri’, a work that exposed caste oppression and advocated social reform in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jyotirao Phule.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gulamgiri (गुलामगिरी, meaning "Slavery") was written by Jyotirao (Jyotiba) Phule in 1873. It is a book in Marathi that criticised caste oppression and Brahmanical domination, and compared the condition of the lower castes in India with that of slaves in America.

 

• He dedicated the book to the Black Americans who fought against slavery in the American Civil War.

 

• Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 in Pune, and started the first school for girls in Pune in 1848 along with his wife Savitribai Phule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other works of Phule: *Tritiya Ratna* (1855), *Shetkaryacha Asud* (1881, "Cultivator's Whipcord") and *Sarvajanik Satyadharma* (published after his death).

 

• He was given the title "Mahatma" in 1888. Ambedkar considered Phule one of his three gurus (along with Buddha and Kabir).

 

NOTE

 

• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar (Option 1) is wrong: his famous works include *Annihilation of Caste* (1936) and *The Buddha and His Dhamma*.

 

• Periyar E.V. Ramasamy (Option 3) is wrong: he led the Self-Respect Movement (1925) in Tamil Nadu.

 

• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar (Option 4) is wrong: he worked for widow remarriage (Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856).

question: Who among the following personalities was the architect behind the design of the Indian National Flag?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pingali Venkayya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pingali Venkayya (पिंगली वेंकैया) (1876–1963), a freedom fighter from Andhra Pradesh, is the designer of the Indian National Flag. question: x and y are positive integers such that x⁴ + y⁴ + x²y² = 473 and xy = 16, then what is the value of x² + xy + y²?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 43.

GIVEN

• x⁴ + y⁴ + x²y² = 473 and xy = 16. Find x² + xy + y².

SOLUTION

• Use the identity: x⁴ + y⁴ + x²y² = (x² + xy + y²)(x² − xy + y²).

• Let a = x² + y². Then (a + 16)(a − 16) = 473, so a² − 256 = 473.

• a² = 729, so a = 27 (positive).

• x² + xy + y² = 27 + 16 = 43.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Remember x⁴ + x²y² + y⁴ = (x² + xy + y²)(x² − xy + y²). The two factors differ by 2xy = 32, and 43 × 11 = 473, so the factors are 43 and 11 (difference 32). ✓

NOTE

• Options 52, 15 and 37 do not satisfy (p)(p − 32) = 473 for the factor p = x² + xy + y².

• (Flagged: the statement says x, y are integers, but no integers give x² + y² = 27 with xy = 16; the algebra still gives 43, which is the key.)

question: Ram, Ravi, Rahim started a business. Ram invests 37.5% of the total capital, Ravi invested 66⅔% of the remaining capital and the Rahim invested the rest. If the total profit at the end of the year was Rs. 2,040 then find the amount by which the profit Ravi exceeds Raheem?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Rs. 425.

GIVEN

• Ram = 37.5% = 3/8 of the capital. Ravi = 66⅔% = 2/3 of the remaining. Rahim = the rest. Profit = Rs. 2,040.

SOLUTION

• Take total capital = 24 units. Ram = 3/8 × 24 = 9. Remaining = 15.

• Ravi = 2/3 × 15 = 10. Rahim = 15 − 10 = 5.

• Ratio Ram : Ravi : Rahim = 9 : 10 : 5 (total 24 parts).

• 1 part of profit = 2,040 ÷ 24 = Rs. 85.

• Ravi − Rahim = (10 − 5) × 85 = 5 × 85 = Rs. 425.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• The time is the same for everybody, so profit is in the ratio of capital. Difference 5 parts × 85 = 425.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Rs. 375) = 4.4 parts, not a whole number of parts.

• Option 3 (Rs. 500) and Option 4 (Rs. 575) do not match 5 parts (425).

• Ram's profit = 9 × 85 = 765; Ravi = 850; Rahim = 425; the total is 2,040. ✓

question: A certain sum of money is invested at a rate of 16.67% per annum, with the interest being compounded annually. After being invested for 3 years, the amount accumulated becomes ₹15,000. Find the amount at the end of the 4th year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ₹17,500.

GIVEN

• Rate = 16.67% = 1/6 per annum (compound). Amount after 3 years = ₹15,000. Find the amount after 4 years.

SOLUTION

• The amount grows each year by a factor of 1 + 1/6 = 7/6.

• Amount after 4 years = amount after 3 years × 7/6.

• = 15,000 × 7/6 = 2,500 × 7 = ₹17,500.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Amount of 4th year = A₃ + 1/6 of A₃ = 15,000 + 2,500 = 17,500. No need to find the principal.

NOTE

• Option 1 (₹18,500) is wrong: it is not 15,000 × 7/6.

• Option 3 (₹17,000) and Option 4 (₹17,250) are wrong: they correspond to rates of 13.33% and 15%.

• Formula: A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ; the next-year amount = present amount × (1 + r/100).

question: The cost price of two articles A and B is the same. Article A is sold at a loss of 30% and Article B is sold for Rs. 2,300 more than the selling price of A. If the net profit made by selling both the articles together is 16%, then what is the selling price of article B?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Rs. 4,050.

GIVEN

• CP of A = CP of B = c. SP of A = 70% of c. SP of B = SP of A + Rs. 2,300. Overall profit = 16%.

SOLUTION

• Total CP = 2c. Total SP = 2c × 1.16 = 2.32c.

• SP of A + SP of B = 0.7c + (0.7c + 2,300) = 1.4c + 2,300.

• 1.4c + 2,300 = 2.32c, so 0.92c = 2,300 and c = Rs. 2,500.

• SP of A = 0.7 × 2,500 = 1,750. SP of B = 1,750 + 2,300 = Rs. 4,050.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• The extra 2,300 equals the gap between 2.32c and 1.4c, i.e. 0.92c, so c = 2,500 at once. SP of B = 2,500 × 1.62 = 4,050 (profit of 62% on B).

NOTE

• Option 1 (Rs. 5,400), Option 2 (Rs. 4,250) and Option 4 (Rs. 4,500) do not satisfy SP(A) + SP(B) = 2.32c with SP(B) − SP(A) = 2,300.

• Check: total SP = 1,750 + 4,050 = 5,800 = 116% of 5,000. ✓

question: A milk man mixes 40lit of water with 80 lit of milk. After selling 25% of this mixture, he adds water to replenish quantity that he has sold. What is the current proportion of water to milk?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 1:1.

GIVEN

• Water = 40 L, milk = 80 L, total = 120 L. 25% of the mixture is sold and the same quantity of water is added.

SOLUTION

• Initial ratio water : milk = 40 : 80 = 1 : 2.

• Quantity sold = 25% of 120 = 30 L, taken out in the ratio 1 : 2, so water removed = 10 L and milk removed = 20 L.

• Left: water = 40 − 10 = 30 L, milk = 80 − 20 = 60 L.

• Water added = 30 L, so water = 30 + 30 = 60 L, milk = 60 L.

• Water : milk = 60 : 60 = 1 : 1.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Milk left = 80 × 3/4 = 60 L. The new water = 120 − 60 = 60 L (total quantity is restored to 120 L). So the ratio is 60 : 60 = 1 : 1.

NOTE

• Option 1 (2 : 1) and Option 4 (2 : 3) would need the milk to be different from 60 L.

• Option 2 (1 : 2) is the ratio before the sale, not after adding the water.

• Formula: when a fraction f of a mixture is removed, each part falls to (1 − f) of its original quantity.

question: In an examination 70% of the students passed in Arithmetic, 55% of the students passed in Reasoning, 20% of the students failed in both the subjects. 125 students who passed only in Arithmetic, then find how many students failed only in reasoning?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 125.

GIVEN

• Passed Arithmetic = 70%, passed Reasoning = 55%, failed both = 20%. Students who passed only in Arithmetic = 125.

SOLUTION

• Passed at least one subject = 100% − 20% = 80%.

• Passed both = 70% + 55% − 80% = 45%.

• Only Arithmetic = 70% − 45% = 25%, and this is 125 students, so the total = 500.

• Failed only in Reasoning means the student passed Arithmetic but failed Reasoning, which is the same group as "only Arithmetic" = 25% of 500 = 125.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• "Failed only in Reasoning" = "passed only in Arithmetic" (the student must have passed the other subject), so the answer is the given 125 directly.

NOTE

• Option 1 (145), Option 2 (120) and Option 4 (225) do not match any region of the Venn diagram (only Reasoning = 10% = 50, both = 225, none = 100).

• Formula: n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B).

question: Train A takes 1 ½ hours more than train B to cover a distance of 240 km. If the speed of train A doubles, it then takes 30 minutes less than the time taken by train B for the same distance. What is the speed of train B?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 96 kmph.

GIVEN

• Distance = 240 km. Time of A = time of B + 1.5 h. When A's speed doubles, time of A = time of B − 0.5 h.

SOLUTION

• Let B's time = t hours. A's time = t + 1.5 h.

• With double speed, A's time becomes (t + 1.5) ÷ 2.

• (t + 1.5) ÷ 2 = t − 0.5, so t + 1.5 = 2t − 1 and t = 2.5 h.

• Speed of B = 240 ÷ 2.5 = 96 km/h.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Check: A takes 4 h (speed 60), doubled speed 120 gives 2 h, which is 0.5 h less than B's 2.5 h. ✓

NOTE

• Option 1 (100): time 2.4 h, so A would take 3.9 h and with double speed 1.95 h, not 1.9 h. ✗

• Option 2 (84) and Option 4 (72) do not satisfy both conditions.

• Formula: time = distance ÷ speed; doubling the speed halves the time.

question: Ravi is thrice as good as work man as Krishna. If together they can complete a work in 28 days, in how many days Ravi alone completes the work?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 37.33 days.

GIVEN

• Efficiency of Ravi : Krishna = 3 : 1. Together they take 28 days.

SOLUTION

• Total work = (3 + 1) × 28 = 112 units.

• Ravi alone = 112 ÷ 3 = 37.33 days (37⅓ days).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Time is inversely proportional to efficiency. Ravi's time = 28 × 4/3 = 37.33 days; Krishna's time = 28 × 4 = 112 days.

NOTE

• Option 2 (45.25) and Option 3 (39) do not follow from 28 × 4/3.

• Option 4 (28 days) is the time taken together, not Ravi alone.

• Formula: if A is n times as efficient as B, then A takes 1/n of B's time.

question: The ratio of efficiency of P & Q is 9:5. Working together they can complete a certain work in 7½ days. P alone completed the 3/7 part of the work and after which Q alone completed the remaining work. The total number of days in which the entire work got complete is?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 17 days.

GIVEN

• Efficiency P : Q = 9 : 5. Together they take 7½ days. P does 3/7 of the work, then Q finishes the rest.

SOLUTION

• Total work = (9 + 5) × 7.5 = 105 units.

• P's part = 3/7 × 105 = 45 units, taking 45 ÷ 9 = 5 days.

• Remaining work = 105 − 45 = 60 units, done by Q in 60 ÷ 5 = 12 days.

• Total days = 5 + 12 = 17 days.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Time of P alone for the whole work = 105 ÷ 9 = 11⅔ days, so 3/7 of it = 5 days. Time of Q alone = 21 days, so 4/7 of it = 12 days. Total 17.

NOTE

• Option 1 (12 days) is only Q's part, not the total.

• Option 2 (15 days) and Option 4 (18 days) do not match 5 + 12.

• Formula: Total work = (sum of efficiencies) × time taken together.

question: If 3x = a + b + c, find the value of (x - a)³ + (x - b)³ + (x - c)³ - 3(x - a)(x - b)(x - c).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 0.

GIVEN

• 3x = a + b + c. Find (x − a)³ + (x − b)³ + (x − c)³ − 3(x − a)(x − b)(x − c).

SOLUTION

• Let p = x − a, q = x − b, r = x − c. The expression is p³ + q³ + r³ − 3pqr.

• p + q + r = 3x − (a + b + c) = 0.

• Identity: p³ + q³ + r³ − 3pqr = (p + q + r)(p² + q² + r² − pq − qr − rp).

• Since p + q + r = 0, the value = 0 × (…) = 0.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• If a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc, so a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = 0. Here the three terms (x − a), (x − b), (x − c) sum to zero.

NOTE

• Option 1 (a + b + c) and Option 4 (a + b − c) are wrong: the factor (p + q + r) is zero, so the product is zero.

• Option 2 ((a − b)(b − c)(c − a)) is wrong: it does not appear in this identity.

• Formula: a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca).

question: If x : y : z = 5 : 6 : 7 and 3x−2y + z = 40, then the value of z is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 28.

GIVEN

• x : y : z = 5 : 6 : 7 and 3x − 2y + z = 40.

SOLUTION

• Let x = 5k, y = 6k, z = 7k.

• 3(5k) − 2(6k) + 7k = 15k − 12k + 7k = 10k = 40, so k = 4.

• z = 7k = 7 × 4 = 28.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Substitute the ratio terms directly: 3×5 − 2×6 + 7 = 10 corresponds to 40, so one ratio unit = 4. Then z = 7 × 4 = 28.

NOTE

• Option 1 (14) is 7 × 2 (it would give 3x − 2y + z = 20). ✗

• Option 2 (22) and Option 4 (18) are not multiples of 7, but z must be 7k. ✗

• Formula: if a : b : c is given, write them as ak, bk, ck and solve for k.

question: What is the least number that must be subtracted from 9400 to make it divisible by 23?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 16.

GIVEN

• Number = 9400. Divisor = 23. Find the least number to subtract so that it becomes divisible by 23.

SOLUTION

• Divide 9400 by 23: 23 × 408 = 9,384.

• Remainder = 9,400 − 9,384 = 16.

• The least number to subtract is the remainder = 16. (9400 − 16 = 9384 = 23 × 408.)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• 23 × 400 = 9200; the left part 200 = 23 × 8 + 16 (23 × 8 = 184), so the remainder is 16.

NOTE

• Option 2 (18): 9400 − 18 = 9382, which is not divisible by 23. ✗

• Option 3 (24) is greater than the divisor 23, so it cannot be the least number to subtract. ✗

• Option 4 (20): 9400 − 20 = 9380, which is not divisible by 23. ✗

• Rule: the least number to subtract = remainder; the least number to add = divisor − remainder (here 23 − 16 = 7).

The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 1/3.

GIVEN

• Expression: √(0.4̅) × (0.46̅ + 0.03̅), where the bar is over the repeating digit (0.444…, 0.4666…, 0.0333…).

SOLUTION

• 0.4̅ = 4/9, so √(4/9) = 2/3.

• 0.46̅ = (46 − 4)/90 = 42/90 = 7/15.

• 0.03̅ = (3 − 0)/90 = 3/90 = 1/30.

• 0.46̅ + 0.03̅ = 7/15 + 1/30 = 14/30 + 1/30 = 15/30 = 1/2.

• Value = 2/3 × 1/2 = 1/3.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Pure recurring: 0.a̅ = a/9. Mixed recurring: 0.ab̅ = (ab − a)/90.

NOTE

• Option 1 (1/5), Option 2 (1/7) and Option 4 (1/2): none equals 2/3 × 1/2. (1/2 is only the bracket value.) ✗

• (Reading note: the repeating bars are read from the printed question: over 4, over 6 and over 3.)

The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 2.

GIVEN

• Expression: [(2.3)³ − 0.027] ÷ [(2.3)² + 0.69 + 0.09].

SOLUTION

• 0.027 = (0.3)³, 0.69 = 2.3 × 0.3 and 0.09 = (0.3)².

• So the expression is (a³ − b³) ÷ (a² + ab + b²) with a = 2.3 and b = 0.3.

• Using a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²), the value = a − b = 2.3 − 0.3 = 2.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Whenever you see (a³ − b³) ÷ (a² + ab + b²), the answer is simply (a − b). Similarly (a³ + b³) ÷ (a² − ab + b²) = (a + b).

NOTE

• Option 2 (7), Option 3 (1) and Option 4 (9) are wrong: a − b = 2.0, not any of these.

• Formula: a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 3.

GIVEN

• Expression: √(6 + √(6 + √(6 + … ∞))).

SOLUTION

• Let x = √(6 + √(6 + …)). Since the pattern repeats forever, x = √(6 + x).

• Square both sides: x² = 6 + x, so x² − x − 6 = 0.

• Factorise: (x − 3)(x + 2) = 0, so x = 3 or x = −2. A square root is positive, so x = 3.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• For √(n + √(n + …)), find two consecutive numbers whose product is n: 6 = 3 × 2, so the answer is the larger one, 3. (For 12 = 4 × 3, the answer is 4.)

NOTE

• Option 1 (6): √(6 + 6) = √12 ≈ 3.46 ≠ 6. ✗

• Option 3 (8): √(6 + 8) = √14 ≈ 3.74 ≠ 8. ✗

• Option 4 (9): √(6 + 9) = √15 ≈ 3.87 ≠ 9. ✗

• Check: √(6 + 3) = √9 = 3. ✓

question: A right prism has a square base of side 9 cm and height 20 cm. Find its total surface area.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 882 cm².

GIVEN

• Base = square of side 9 cm, height = 20 cm.

SOLUTION

• Total surface area = 2 × (base area) + (perimeter of base × height).

• Base area = 9 × 9 = 81 cm², so 2 × 81 = 162 cm².

• Lateral surface area = 4 × 9 × 20 = 720 cm².

• TSA = 162 + 720 = 882 cm².

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• The prism is a cuboid 9 × 9 × 20: TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl) = 2(81 + 180 + 180) = 2 × 441 = 882.

NOTE

• Option 1 (720 cm²) is only the lateral surface area, without the two bases.

• Option 2 (801 cm²) and Option 4 (900 cm²) do not match 162 + 720. ✗

• Formula: TSA of a right prism = lateral area (perimeter × height) + 2 × base area.

question: If a = √3481 and b = √2209, then find the value of (a² − b²) ÷ (a − b).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 106.

GIVEN

• a = √3481, b = √2209. Find (a² − b²) ÷ (a − b).

SOLUTION

• (a² − b²) ÷ (a − b) = (a + b)(a − b) ÷ (a − b) = a + b.

• √3481 = 59 (59 × 59 = 3,481) and √2209 = 47 (47 × 47 = 2,209).

• a + b = 59 + 47 = 106.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Perfect squares ending in 1 have roots ending in 1 or 9; 59² = 3481. Ending in 9 has roots ending in 3 or 7; 47² = 2209.

NOTE

• Option 1 (96), Option 2 (104) and Option 4 (112) are wrong: a + b = 59 + 47 = 106.

• Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).

question: If sec(7θ − 11°) = cosec(4θ + 2°), where both angles are acute, then θ is equal to:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 9°.

GIVEN

• sec(7θ − 11°) = cosec(4θ + 2°), both angles acute.

SOLUTION

• cosec A = sec(90° − A), so cosec(4θ + 2°) = sec(90° − 4θ − 2°) = sec(88° − 4θ).

• Equate the angles: 7θ − 11° = 88° − 4θ, so 11θ = 99° and θ = 9°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• sec A = cosec B with A, B acute means A + B = 90°. So (7θ − 11) + (4θ + 2) = 90, i.e. 11θ − 9 = 90 and θ = 9°.

NOTE

• Check: 7θ − 11 = 52° and 4θ + 2 = 38°, and 52° + 38° = 90°. ✓

• Option 1 (7°): angles 38° and 30°, sum 68°. ✗

• Option 2 (8°): angles 45° and 34°, sum 79°. ✗

• Option 4 (10°): angles 59° and 42°, sum 101°. ✗

• Remember: sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ, sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ.

question: A cuboid has dimensions 10 cm, 6 cm and 4 cm. What is its total surface area?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 248 cm².

GIVEN

• Length = 10 cm, breadth = 6 cm, height = 4 cm.

SOLUTION

• TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl).

• lb = 10 × 6 = 60, bh = 6 × 4 = 24, hl = 4 × 10 = 40.

• Sum = 60 + 24 + 40 = 124, so TSA = 2 × 124 = 248 cm².

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Add the three face-pair areas first and then double: 124 × 2 = 248.

NOTE

• Option 1 (200 cm²) and Option 2 (224 cm²) and Option 4 (280 cm²) are wrong: they come from missing or adding a face pair.

• Option 1 = 2(60 + 40) = 200 (leaves out the 6 × 4 faces). ✗

• Formulae: volume = lbh = 240 cm³; lateral surface = 2h(l + b) = 128 cm²; diagonal = √(l² + b² + h²) = √152.

question: A regular square pyramid has base side 10 cm and slant height 13 cm. What is its lateral surface area?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 260 cm².

GIVEN

• Base side = 10 cm (square), slant height = 13 cm.

SOLUTION

• Lateral surface area = ½ × (perimeter of base) × (slant height).

• Perimeter = 4 × 10 = 40 cm.

• LSA = ½ × 40 × 13 = 260 cm².

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Four triangular faces, each ½ × 10 × 13 = 65, so 4 × 65 = 260.

NOTE

• Option 1 (130 cm²) is the area of two triangular faces only. ✗

• Option 2 (200 cm²) uses 40 × 10 ÷ 2, i.e. the wrong height. ✗

• Option 4 (360 cm²) = 260 + 100 is the total surface area (it includes the base). ✗

• Formula: LSA of a regular pyramid = ½ × perimeter × slant height; TSA = LSA + base area.

question: If sin²θ = 9/25 and cosθ is positive, then the value of sin²θ + cos²θ is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 1.

GIVEN

• sin²θ = 9/25, cos θ > 0.

SOLUTION

• The identity sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 holds for every angle θ.

• Check: cos²θ = 1 − 9/25 = 16/25, so sin²θ + cos²θ = 9/25 + 16/25 = 25/25 = 1.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• No calculation is needed: the sum of squares of sine and cosine of the same angle is always 1.

NOTE

• Option 1 (9/25) is only sin²θ. ✗

• Option 2 (16/25) is only cos²θ. ✗

• Option 4 (25/16) is 1 ÷ cos²θ = sec²θ. ✗

• Identities: 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ. (Here sin θ = 3/5, cos θ = 4/5, a 3-4-5 triangle.)

question: In a cyclic quadrilateral, two opposite angles are (2x + 10)° and (3x − 5)°. Find the larger of these two opposite angles.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 100°.

GIVEN

• Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral: (2x + 10)° and (3x − 5)°.

SOLUTION

• Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary (sum = 180°).

• (2x + 10) + (3x − 5) = 180, so 5x + 5 = 180 and x = 35.

• Angles: 2(35) + 10 = 80° and 3(35) − 5 = 100°.

• The larger angle = 100°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Add the constants and the x-terms: 5x + 5 = 180, so x = 35. The bigger coefficient (3x) gives the larger angle: 105 − 5 = 100.

NOTE

• Option 1 (70°): the opposite angle would be 110°, which cannot be one of these two angles. ✗

• Option 2 (80°) is the smaller angle (2x + 10). ✗

• Option 3 (90°): it would make both angles 90°, which needs x = 40 and x = 31.67, a contradiction. ✗

• Property: opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°; an exterior angle equals the interior opposite angle.

question: Simplify: (cosec A − cot A)² + (cosec A + cot A)² − 4cot² A.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 2.

GIVEN

• Expression = (cosec A − cot A)² + (cosec A + cot A)² − 4cot²A.

SOLUTION

• Use (p − q)² + (p + q)² = 2(p² + q²), with p = cosec A and q = cot A.

• Expression = 2cosec²A + 2cot²A − 4cot²A = 2cosec²A − 2cot²A.

• = 2(cosec²A − cot²A) = 2 × 1 = 2.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Use the identity cosec²A − cot²A = 1; the whole expression becomes 2(cosec²A − cot²A) = 2.

NOTE

• Option 1 (0) would need cosec²A = cot²A, which is never true. ✗

• Option 2 (1) forgets the factor 2 from the sum of squares. ✗

• Option 4 (4) is wrong: 2(cosec²A − cot²A) = 2, not 4.

• Identities: sin²A + cos²A = 1; 1 + cot²A = cosec²A; 1 + tan²A = sec²A.

question: A closed hemispherical dome has radius 6 cm. Its total surface area includes the curved surface and circular base. What is the total surface area?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 108π cm².

GIVEN

• Hemisphere of radius r = 6 cm, with the curved surface and the circular base.

SOLUTION

• Curved surface area = 2πr² = 2π × 36 = 72π cm².

• Base area = πr² = 36π cm².

• Total surface area = 3πr² = 72π + 36π = 108π cm².

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Total surface area of a solid hemisphere = 3πr². With r = 6, 3 × 36 = 108, so 108π.

NOTE

• Option 1 (72π cm²) is only the curved surface area (2πr²). ✗

• Option 2 (96π cm²) does not match any hemisphere formula for r = 6. ✗

• Option 4 (144π cm²) = 4πr², the surface area of a full sphere. ✗

• Formulae: sphere = 4πr²; hemisphere (curved) = 2πr²; hemisphere (total) = 3πr²; volume of hemisphere = (2/3)πr³.

question:

• Loose (adjective) means not tight or not firmly fixed: "a loose shirt".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

• Option 3: "even when provoked" is correct; the subject and the auxiliary are understood ("even when I am provoked").

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part which contains a grammatical error (ignore any punctuation error, if any). If there is no error in the sentence, then select 'No Error'.

(a) Not only did the CEO's controversial statement/ (b) led to a sharp decline in the company's stock price, / (c) but it also permanently damaged the brand's reputation. / (d) No error.
option_1: Not only did the CEO's controversial statement
option_2: led to a sharp decline in the company's stock price
option_3: but it also permanently damaged the brand's reputation
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. led to a sharp decline in the company's stock price.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The error is in part (b): after "did" (inverted auxiliary) the main verb must be in its base form. So "led to" should be "lead to".

 

• Rule: In a "Not only did + subject + verb" sentence (inversion), the auxiliary "did" carries the tense, and the verb that follows takes the first form.

◦ Correct: Not only did the CEO's controversial statement lead to a sharp decline in the company's stock price, but it also permanently damaged the brand's reputation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "Not only did the CEO's controversial statement" is correct as the start of the inversion.

 

• Option 3: "but it also permanently damaged the brand's reputation" is correct: past tense after "but", which is not under the inversion.

 

• Option 4: "No error" is wrong because of "led" in part (b).

 

NOTE

 

• Similar rule: "Hardly had he arrived when…"; "Never did I see…"; "Rarely does he complain." After did/does/do, use the base verb.

question:

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. is constantly pondering over.
