• The underlined segment "is constantly ponder about" is wrong: after "is" the verb must be in the -ing form (present continuous), so "pondering". "Look at…" also suggests an action happening right now.

 

• The verb ponder is used as "ponder over" or "ponder on" (or directly with an object: "ponder the question"), so the correct segment is "is constantly pondering over", as per the PDF key.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "is constantly pondering about" has the right tense but the wrong preposition; "ponder" is not used with "about".

 

• Option 2: "constantly ponders about" uses the simple present, which does not suit "Look at…" (an action in progress), and it also uses "about".

 

• Option 4: "No improvement" is wrong because "is … ponder" is ungrammatical.

 

NOTE

 

• (Flagged: "ponder" can also be used without a preposition; the key follows the PDF, which marks "pondering over".)

 

• Present continuous: is/am/are + verb-ing.

question:
Select the grammatically correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.

The young pianist practiced so diligent that her fingers moved across the keys with a grace that left the audience breathless.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. diligently that her fingers moved.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Practiced" is a verb, so it must be modified by an adverb, not an adjective. "Diligent" (adjective) must become "diligently" (adverb).

 

• The structure is "so + adverb + that + clause". The tense of the clause must match the past tense "practiced": "her fingers moved".

◦ Correct: The young pianist practiced so diligently that her fingers moved across the keys…

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "diligently that her fingers move" has the right adverb, but "move" (present) does not agree with the past tense "practiced".

 

• Option 3: "diligent that her fingers move" keeps the adjective and the wrong tense, so it is wrong twice.

 

• Option 4: "No improvement" is wrong because "diligent" cannot modify the verb "practiced".

 

NOTE

 

• Rule: Adjectives describe nouns; adverbs describe verbs, adjectives or other adverbs. Pattern: so + adjective/adverb + that (result clause).

question:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill in the blank in the given sentence.

He was very tired, ___ he continued to work until midnight.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. yet.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The two clauses show contrast: he was tired, but he still continued to work. The conjunction that shows contrast is "yet" (= but, still).

◦ Correct: He was very tired, yet he continued to work until midnight.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: so shows a result (He was tired, so he slept). The sentence needs contrast, not result.

 

• Option 3: because gives a reason; it would mean he worked because he was tired, which is illogical.

 

• Option 4: or gives a choice or alternative, which does not fit.

 

NOTE

 

• Contrast conjunctions: but, yet, still, however, although, though, whereas.

question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

P. Finally, they burst crackers joyfully in the street and exchanged gifts with all their neighbours.

Q. Amita and Aman spent the afternoon carefully arranging sweets in decorative boxes for distribution.

R. As dusk fell on Diwali evening, they lit rows of earthen diyas along the courtyard and doorstep.

solution_text:

question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

P. Shivam opened every cabinet and shelf and noted down which essential items had completely run out.

Q. Back home, he unpacked all the shopping bags and stored each item neatly in its correct place.

R. He walked through the supermarket aisle by aisle and collected every item from his written list.

S. He then sat at the kitchen table and wrote out a clear and complete shopping list.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. PSRQ.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The logical story: check what is needed (P), write the list (S: "He then sat…"), shop from the list (R), come home and store the items (Q: "Back home…").

 

• So the correct order is P → S → R → Q.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (RSPQ) starts with shopping before the list is written, which is illogical.

 

• Option 3 (QPSR) starts with "Back home", which cannot come first, because the shopping has not been mentioned yet.

 

• Option 4 (PRQS) goes shopping (R) before writing the list (S), and the list is written after he returns, which breaks the sense.

 

NOTE

 

• Look for linkers: "then" refers back to a previous action (S follows P), and "Back home" must follow a trip (Q follows R).

question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

P. This duality suggests that every refined gentleman hides a primitive, darker side.

Q. He eventually transforms into the monstrous Mr Hyde to indulge his forbidden desires.

R. Dr Jekyll is a respected scientist who struggles with his own internal conflicts.

S. To separate his good side from his evil impulses, he creates a powerful chemical potion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. RSQP.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• R introduces the main character, Dr Jekyll, and his inner conflict, so it is the opening sentence.

 

• S: "To separate his good side…, he creates a potion" follows from his conflict. Q: "He eventually transforms into Mr Hyde" is the result of the potion. P: "This duality suggests…" sums up the idea, so it is the closing sentence.

 

• The correct order is R → S → Q → P.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (QPSR) starts with "He eventually transforms", but nobody has been introduced yet.

 

• Option 2 (SQRP) starts with "he creates", where "he" is not yet identified.

 

• Option 3 (RPQS) places the conclusion ("This duality suggests…") before the story of the potion and the transformation, so it breaks the sequence.

 

NOTE

 

• Look for the introduced noun (Dr Jekyll) before the pronoun (he), and a concluding word like "duality" or "thus" for the last line.

question:
In the following sentence, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which gives the correct meaning of the underlined idiom or phrase.

The artist’s sudden fame proved to be a flash in the pan as his second gallery was a total failure.
option_1: A sudden but very brief success period
option_2: A permanent change in a person's life
option_3: A dangerous fire in a kitchen area
option_4: A very bright light in a dark room
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A sudden but very brief success period.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A flash in the pan (idiom) means something that shows great promise at first but then fails or is short-lived; a sudden but very brief success. (क्षणिक सफलता, पल भर की चमक)

◦ Example: His first film was a flash in the pan, and he never had another hit.

 

• Origin: in old flintlock guns the powder in the pan flashed without firing the gun.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "A permanent change" is the opposite of the idiom, which stresses brevity.

 

• Option 3: "A dangerous fire in a kitchen area" takes "pan" literally.

 

• Option 4: "A very bright light in a dark room" takes "flash" literally.

 

NOTE

 

• Related idioms: a nine-day wonder, a one-hit wonder, a flash in the pan = a short-lived success.

question:
Choose the option that contains the homonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The museum curator carefully placed the ancient gold object into the glass display case to protect it from dust.
option_1: During the deep-sea dive, the explorers spotted a metallic object partially buried in the sand near the shipwreck.
option_2: The science teacher explained that every solid object in the room is made up of millions of tiny atoms.
option_3: Although the plan seemed efficient, several board members decided to object to the high cost of the new project.
option_4: When the light hit the crystalline object on the shelf, it created a beautiful rainbow across the opposite wall.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Although the plan seemed efficient, several board members decided to object to the high cost of the new project..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A homonym is a word with the same spelling (and often the same sound) as another word but a different meaning. In the question, "object" is a noun (a thing). The homonym is "object" used as a verb, meaning to disagree or protest, as in "decided to object to the high cost" (Option 3). (आपत्ति करना)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 all use "object" as a noun meaning a thing, the same meaning as in the question, so none is a homonym.

 

NOTE

 

• Homonym = same spelling or sound, different meanings (bat, bank, bear). Homophone = same sound, different spelling (to/too). Homograph = same spelling, different sound or meaning (lead, object: OB-ject / ob-JECT).

question:
Complete the following passage by filling in the blanks with the most appropriate words from the options given below.

 

The Gothic cathedral was never intended to be merely a shelter or a place of assembly; it was a stone encyclopedia meant to be "read" by the illiterate masses. In an age where books were rare and literacy was a privilege (A)_____ the elite, the church used architecture to communicate theology. Every carving, window and arch was a word in a silent sermon.

 

Every spire reaching toward the heavens and every grotesque gargoyle perched on the eaves conveyed a specific theological or moral message. The heights inspired awe and humility, while the frightening figures served as reminders of the spiritual dangers (B)_____ outside the sacred space. It was an immersive experience designed to bypass the intellect and speak directly to the soul.

 

To the medieval mind, the cathedral would have represented the physical bridge between the celestial and the terrestrial. Standing in the nave, bathed in the "divine light" of stained glass, the peasant felt a proximity to the divine that was (C)_____ unavailable. The building was a portal, a physical manifestation of the Kingdom of Heaven on Earth.

 

Because the structural innovations, like the flying buttress, allowed for towering heights and thinner walls, the primary intent remained spiritual rather than technical. The engineering was a (D)_____ to an end – the creation of a space that felt unburdened by the weight of the world. The triumph of light over stone was a metaphor for the triumph of the spirit over the flesh.

 

However, this intricate architectural language remains impenetrable to those who lack a (E)_____ in medieval symbolism. Modern visitors often see the beauty but miss the "text". To truly understand the Gothic style, one must learn to look at the stone not just as a material, but as a medium of complex, coded communication.

 

Choose the preposition to collocate with the word “privilege” and fill in the blank (A).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. of.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct preposition is "of": a privilege of the elite (the privilege belonging to a particular group). Here "literacy was a privilege of the elite" means only the elite could read.

◦ Example: Higher education was once a privilege of the rich.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: for ("a privilege for the elite") is not the standard collocation here; "for" is used as "a privilege for me to speak".

 

• Option 3: to is used as "the privilege to vote" (before a verb or a right), not before a group of people.

 

• Option 4: by ("privilege by the elite") would mean the privilege was done by them, which is wrong.

 

NOTE

 

• Collocations: a privilege of (a group), the privilege of doing something, the privilege to do something, a privilege to be here.
